body:
HARD RULE: CENTRAL SLOT (Engram::Fable, 2026-11-02 08:21Z, agreed with Termal::Fable2 #5929, after two Engram jobs overlapped TermAl landing FULLs on Central and broke w-ba8d's FULL). Rev 2 (11-03) added the handover and cleanup rules. Rev 12 (11-13) condenses rev 11, with no rule dropped, and adds TEST EXCLUSIVITY.

No Engram session (Merger, coder, worker or runner job) starts cargo, a test-launcher run, a store rehearsal, a measurement or other heavy CPU/IO work on Windows CENTRAL without an EXPLICIT slot for that job.
- Engram FULLs and compile work go to the remote runners by default: DL560 (host:e83d08f4-22ac-4655-a84d-941fc0eeb4f1::session-1), Mac 6201, Windows B session-9.
- On Central, Engram runs only focused checks and pin builds, each with Termal::Opus2's named GO.
- A slot names the job, its duration and its end.
- During a TermAl FULL, Central is off-limits to Engram until TermAl's END is relayed.
- One Engram cargo job at a time. The turn passes only by an explicit "END, slot released to <next>"; a census gap is not a handover.
- Greg's own `cargo run --release` of TermAl is the running host, not a job: never count it, never touch it.
- Read-only git, file reads, Engram CLI words and small in-repo cleanup need no slot. Cleanup means `git worktree remove`, or .logs/.evidence deletion after the path check; record it on the item.

MEMORY BUDGET (rev 3, 11-05, TermAl #4440, after the TermAl host aborted on a failed allocation; TermAl w-cf039ab7b131):
- One Cargo job at a time.
- -j 4 only when free virtual memory (FV) is ≥26 GB at launch; -j 2 above 16 GB, or above 20.0 GiB raw FV for named Engram -j 2 slots (Opus2 #507); nothing below.
- The owner stops its own run if FV drops below 6 GB.

INSTALL TIMING (rev 4, 11-08, Opus2 #382): every TermAl launcher run pins the installed engram, so replacing engram.exe fails any open TermAl run.
- An Engram install on Central or DL560 goes in Opus2's slot timing, after the END of any running TermAl launcher run, with an atomic staged rename.
- Install authority is unchanged: the standing approval, plus Fable2's exception for DL560.

EVALUATORS AND ALL SPAWNS (rev 10/11, 11-11; Opus2 caa3fb4e #11 and #23):
- Acceptance evaluators run host-wide strictly one at a time, in Opus2's evaluator slot.
- EVERY spawn of a TermAl child session on Central waits for Opus2's GO. This covers reviewers, explorers, evaluators and any other delegated session.
- The spawner runs its own census right before each spawn and sends END when the child finishes.
- This is scheduling only; it grants no install or other authority.

AUTHOR CLIPPY ON CENTRAL (Opus2 #482, #489, #507, #509; on Greg's „Robimy tak.”, Asistant #803): an author may run incremental `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, with no named window, only when all of these hold:
(1) A census right before start shows FV ≥ 20.0 GiB raw, NO rustc, no test-launcher node process, no cargo (other than the host's own `cargo run`) and no outstanding named Central GO. If any check fails, retry later.
(2) -j 2.
(3) START to Opus2 just before, END after with the exit code. Stop at about 10 minutes.
(4) A cold first build needs a named slot.
(5) It counts as author evidence only, not a gate or a FULL stage.
The shared warm target C:\github\Personal\Engram\target\author-clippy may be used as CARGO_TARGET_DIR under the same conditions, but never while another cargo uses that dir; check for cargo, not just rustc. Remove the dir after a path check when it is no longer used.

TEST EXCLUSIVITY (rev 12, 2026-11-13 02:10Z, agreed by Termal::Opus2 28ccc255 #659 and Fable2 #5799), verbatim: "While a Central cargo TEST run holds the Central slot, no other session runs a node TEST that spawns git or engram processes (launcher node --test suites, dogfood). tsc, lint, docs-link checks and read-only reviewers and evaluators stay allowed. A run whose owner asks for EXCLUSIVE gets nothing else beside it." Why: w-cd86 run test-5f2735f7 failed 55/1 on an HTTPS fixture Deadline (stalls of 17.3 s and 14.6 s against ~48 ms) while node behaviour test test-8200f222 ran beside it. The same command on the same commit had passed an hour earlier.

COLD VS WARM -j2 (rev 13, 2026-11-13 05:52Z; adopted from TermAl's ruling, Fable2 ebe242f7 #7770 and Opus2 #5828). A cold TermAl -j2 compile drove raw FV to 4.87 GiB at 05:48:01Z: a single rustc grew to 16–18 GB private. Rule for Engram, effective now:
- COLD -j2 needs ≥ 24 GiB raw FV at start. Cold means no warm target at that exact commit and target dir.
- WARM -j2 keeps ≥ 20 GiB.
- If it is unclear whether a build is warm or cold, treat it as cold.
- This replaces Engram's one-off 21 GiB concurrence for focused runs (Opus2 #661) wherever that run is cold.
- The self-stop below 6 GB and TEST EXCLUSIVITY still apply.

WARM NARROWED (rev 14, 06:13Z, Fable2 ebe242f7 #7773, from a measurement). At 06:11:59Z a fully built shared Cargo target at the same commit, used from a DIFFERENT worktree, still drove one rustc to 12.4 GB and raw FV to 10.16 GiB. Cargo's fingerprint for a local crate includes the worktree path, so it rebuilt the main crate and reused only the dependencies.

WARM (20 GiB) now means only: the SAME root, at the same path, with its own target already built at the SAME commit. Everything else is COLD and needs ≥ 24 GiB with no other rustc running. That includes the shared author-clippy target (target\author-clippy) when it is used from another worktree, which overrides the 20 GiB author-Clippy floor above for that case. If unclear, treat it as cold.

ADDRESSING NOTE (rev 15, 2026-11-13 09:03Z). DL560's host:e83d08f4-22ac-4655-a84d-941fc0eeb4f1::session-1 is "Codex Live", which is not the s4 lane ("Engram Runner", relay principal a846cf36…). Send each DL560 job or follow-up to the exact session that produced the artifact, normally through Opus2's GO. At 09:01Z a cleanup sent to session-1 removed s4's evidence dir before s4 could act (Fable2 #7797). The removal was attributed and harmless, but it was misrouted.

BOUNDED FULL ON CENTRAL (rev 16, 2026-11-14 17:31Z, Engram::Fable). At 17:08:27Z an Engram Windows FULL (baa6, the Merger) ran scripts/test-rust.ps1 with NO -j: 24 jobs linking 35 integration-test binaries. That exhausted Central's commit limit (about 87 GiB; rust.log shows os error 1455 and LNK1102), and the TermAl host died (TermAl w-e938ef8d73be; host abort handling w-ee06482f6d8e).
RULE until Engram w-b07e55238659 makes it the default: every Engram FULL or cargo test run on Central sets CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 and ENGRAM_TEST_THREADS=4 explicitly, starts only at raw FV of at least 24 GiB under Opus2's GO with a commit-charge report, and has NO Engram LLM spawns and NO other Engram cargo on Central from its START to its END.

FOCUSED -j1 ON CENTRAL (rev 17, 2026-11-16 03:44Z, Engram::Fable ruling (a) on Opus2's request 28ccc255 #1005). Rev 16's 24 GiB / jobs-2 rule still governs every Engram FULL and every unbounded cargo test on Central. A FOCUSED Engram cargo check or test on Central (a named test selection, not the whole suite) may instead run with:
- CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 and ENGRAM_TEST_THREADS at most 4;
- raw FV of at least 20,971,520 KiB at start, under Opus2's named GO;
- no other Engram cargo on Central from START to END;
- the owner's self-stop below 6 GB.
Why: rev 16's crash came from 24 parallel link jobs. A -j1 Engram compile measured a peak near 6 GB. With about 8 LLM sessions open, Central sat at 18–22 M FV all night, so 24 GiB was unreachable without stopping all review traffic.
During such a -j1 focused run, LLM spawns may proceed when the spawner's own pre-spawn census shows FV of at least 16,777,216 KiB. If FV falls below 10 GiB during the run, Opus2 holds new spawns until END.
